games.title: Dhon Dheki
games.description: A rhythmic team game where players sit in two rows and perform coordinated clapping and movement patterns while singing traditional songs.
howToPlay: Step 1: Players sit facing each other in two parallel rows.
Step 2: A leader starts a traditional song with specific rhythm.
Step 3: Players perform synchronized clapping patterns with the song.
Step 4: Movements become faster and more complex as the song progresses.
Step 5: Players who miss a clap or break rhythm are eliminated.
Step 6: The game continues until one row has all players eliminated.
Step 7: Remaining row wins the round.
Step 8: Songs often tell stories or convey cultural messages.
Step 9: Game builds coordination, rhythm, and teamwork.
Step 10: Popular during Eid and other celebrations.

games.title: Hulhavalha
games.description: A traditional hide-and-seek variant played during full moon nights, where seekers use moonlight to find hiders who can move and change positions.
games.occasion: Full moon nights, festivals, community gatherings
howToPlay: Step 1: Players gather in a designated area with good hiding spots.
Step 2: One player is chosen as the seeker and counts to a predetermined number.
Step 3: Other players hide while the seeker counts.
Step 4: Unlike traditional hide-and-seek, hiders can move and change hiding spots.
Step 5: The seeker tries to find and tag hiders using moonlight.
Step 6: Tagged hiders become seekers or are eliminated.
Step 7: Game continues until all hiders are found.
Step 8: Last hider found wins the round.
Step 9: Moonlight adds atmosphere and challenge to the game.
Step 10: Popular during full moon festivals and gatherings.

games.title: Kana Mutti Bindeema
games.description: A traditional game where a blindfolded player attempts to break a clay pot hanging from a height using a long stick, guided by spectators' calls. Tests trust and coordination.
howToPlay: Step 1: A clay pot is filled with water or colored powder and hung from a height.
Step 2: A player is blindfolded and given a long stick.
Step 3: The player is spun around several times to disorient.
Step 4: Spectators shout directions to guide the player toward the pot.
Step 5: The player swings the stick attempting to break the pot.
Step 6: When the pot breaks, contents shower down.
Step 7: Players take turns attempting to break the pot.
Step 8: Requires trust in guidance and spatial awareness.
Step 9: Popular during New Year celebrations.
Step 10: Symbolizes breaking away from the old year.

games.title: Kanamachi (Blind Man's Buff)
games.description: The Bengali version of blind man's buff where one player is blindfolded and tries to catch others, who tease and dodge while singing traditional rhymes.
howToPlay: Step 1: One player is selected as 'Kanamachi' and blindfolded with a cloth.
Step 2: Other players scatter around and tease the blindfolded player.
Step 3: Players sing traditional rhymes while dodging the blindfolded player.
Step 4: The blindfolded player spins around several times before starting.
Step 5: They must rely on sound to locate and tag other players.
Step 6: Other players must stay within a designated play area.
Step 7: When someone is tagged, they become the next blindfolded player.
Step 8: Players can clap or call out to help the blindfolded player locate them.
Step 9: The game teaches spatial awareness and listening skills.
Step 10: Variations include making sounds or giving clues to the seeker.
